# Review Memo — Master Services Agreement (Meridian Fieldworks / Copperleaf Technology)

**Bottom line:** The body of this draft is broadly balanced-to-customer-favorable, but it contains **seven clauses that are grossly off-market against Customer and that directly contradict the customer-friendly provisions elsewhere.** Because they are drafted in absolute terms ("without exception," "without reduction or termination rights," "at Vendor's sole discretion"), a New York court would likely give them effect over the more general language they conflict with. They must be **struck, not negotiated around**. Separately, the draft has a **missing Vendor indemnity, no SLA, a broken cross-reference, and several undrafted sections** that leave Customer without core remedies.

Do not sign in current form.

---

## TIER 1 — Do not execute without these changes

### 1. §2.1 — $6M take-or-pay commitment with no exit *(p0012)*
**Risk:** Binds Customer to USD 2,000,000/year for three years "without reduction or termination rights," irrespective of Vendor's performance. This purports to survive Customer's convenience termination (§9.4), breach termination (§9.1), security-incident termination (§9.3), and force-majeure termination (§27.3), rendering all of them commercially worthless.

**Fix:** Delete §2.1. If a commitment is commercially agreed, replace with:
> "Any minimum volume commitment will be stated in an Order Form. No minimum commitment applies to any period after the effective date of a termination under Sections 9.1, 9.2, 9.3, 9.4 or 27.3, and unused commitment will be credited against amounts otherwise payable."

### 2. §2.2 (first) — Exclusivity for all hosted analytics *(p0013)*
**Risk:** Makes Vendor Customer's sole provider of hosted analytics for three years, with no performance condition and no carve-outs (existing contracts, acquired businesses, Affiliates). Flatly contradicts §12.3, which recites that Customer has made *no* exclusivity commitment.

**Fix:** Delete. This clause is also mis-numbered (two §2.2s) — renumber the survivor.

### 3. §11.1 — Immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination, no exit assistance *(p0045)*
**Risk:** The single most dangerous clause in the document. On any termination — including termination for *Vendor's* breach — Vendor stops all assistance and permanently deletes Customer Data with no export. It contradicts §11.2, §11.3, §10.1 and §10.2, and creates a hostage dynamic in any dispute.

**Fix:** Delete §11.1 and replace:
> "11.1 On Customer's request at any time during the term and for twelve (12) months following expiry or termination (for any reason), Vendor shall provide reasonable transition assistance, including data export, knowledge transfer, and reasonable cooperation with a successor provider, at the rates in the applicable Order Form (or, where termination is for Vendor's breach, at no charge). Vendor shall not delete, degrade, or withhold access to Customer Data during the transition period, and shall not condition transition assistance on payment of disputed amounts or on a release."

### 4. §12.4 — 24-month non-compete on Customer *(p0050)*
**Risk:** Prohibits Customer from developing, marketing, selling **or acquiring** any product or service that competes with Vendor, anywhere, for the term plus two years. This is an extraordinary restraint on Customer's own business and M&A activity, unbounded in scope. Directly contradicts §12.3.

**Fix:** Delete in full. No substitute. (If Vendor pushes back, the most that is arguable is a narrow prohibition on using Vendor's Confidential Information to build a competing product — which §16.2 already covers.)

### 5. §13.1 — Revocable, non-Affiliate, non-contractor licence *(p0052)*
**Risk:** Grants a licence "to Customer alone… revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, without Affiliates or contractors." This (a) makes the entire subscription terminable at will by Vendor, (b) blocks Affiliate and outsourced/MSP use, and (c) contradicts §13.2, §13.3, §24.1 and the Affiliate-ordering premise of §4.

**Fix:** Replace:
> "13.1 Subject to this Agreement, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a worldwide, non-exclusive, irrevocable (during the applicable subscription term) licence to access and use the Services and Documentation for their internal business purposes, including through contractors, service providers, and Authorized Users acting on their behalf, for whose compliance Customer is responsible. Vendor may suspend or revoke access only as expressly permitted by Section 13.3."

### 6. §19.2 — 15-day Deliverable warranty with total remedy cut-off *(p0076)*
**Risk:** "[A]fter that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation." This is a general disclaimer disguised as a warranty period — read literally it also cuts off the ongoing §19.1 conformance warranty and the §19.4 repair/refund remedy for Deliverables.

**Fix:** Replace:
> "19.2 Each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and the applicable acceptance criteria for ninety (90) days after acceptance. The warranty period in this Section does not limit Section 19.1, Section 19.4, or any other remedy available to Customer, and does not operate as a limitation period for any claim."

### 7. §21.1 — One-month fee cap "without exception" *(p0082)*
**Risk:** Caps *all* liability at one month's fees and, via "without exception," overrides the Excluded Claims in §21.3 (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement). On a $2M/year deal that is roughly $167,000 of total exposure for, e.g., a mass data breach. Compounded by §1.5, which excludes implementation charges from "Fees" and therefore shrinks the cap base further.

**Fix:** Replace:
> "21.1 Subject to Sections 21.3 and 21.4, each Party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the greater of (a) USD [—] and (b) the total amounts paid and payable by Customer under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the first event giving rise to the claim. Liability for Excluded Claims is not subject to this cap[, except that Vendor's aggregate liability for breach of its security and data-protection obligations under Sections 15 and 17 will not exceed [3x] the foregoing amount]."

Also amend §1.5 so "Fees" means **all amounts paid or payable by Customer**, including implementation and one-time charges, at least for purposes of the liability cap and refund provisions.

### 8. §20 — No Vendor indemnity at all; unlimited Customer indemnity *(p0080)*
**Risk:** Two structural failures:
- Customer indemnifies Vendor for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services" — including claims caused entirely by Vendor's own defects, negligence, or infringement. This is uncapped (an Excluded Claim under §21.3).
- **There is no Vendor indemnity whatsoever** — no IP infringement defence, no data-breach indemnity, no compliance indemnity. §9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," **which does not exist**, so Customer's IP-infringement termination right is unenforceable as drafted.

**Fix:** Replace Section 20 with a reciprocal structure:
> **20.1 Vendor IP Indemnity.** Vendor shall defend Customer, its Affiliates, and their personnel against any third-party claim that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, or trade secret, and shall indemnify against resulting damages, settlements, and reasonable costs.
> **20.2 Vendor Other Indemnities.** Vendor shall defend and indemnify Customer against third-party claims arising from (a) Vendor's breach of Sections 15, 16 or 17 or a Security Incident affecting Customer Data; (b) Vendor's violation of Applicable Law; (c) death, personal injury, or tangible property damage caused by Vendor; and (d) claims by Vendor personnel or subcontractors relating to their engagement.
> **20.3 Customer Indemnity.** Customer shall defend and indemnify Vendor against third-party claims that Customer Data, as provided by Customer, infringes third-party IP or violates Applicable Law, **except** to the extent arising from Vendor's breach, negligence, or wilful misconduct.
> **20.4 Procedure.** Prompt notice (delay excuses only to the extent of prejudice), indemnitor control of defence with reputable counsel, indemnitee right to participate at its own cost, no settlement imposing liability, admission, or non-monetary obligation on the indemnitee without consent.
> **20.5 Infringement Remedies.** If a claim under 20.1 arises or is reasonably likely, Vendor shall at its expense (a) procure the right to continue use; or (b) modify or replace the item so it is non-infringing with materially equivalent functionality. If neither is achievable within thirty (30) days, either Party may terminate the affected Order Form and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees plus, for perpetual/paid-up items, Fees paid depreciated on a five-year straight-line basis. **Exclusions:** no obligation to the extent infringement arises solely from Customer Data or Customer's unauthorised modification.

This also repairs the §9.3 cross-reference.

---

## TIER 2 — Material gaps

| # | Issue | Risk | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 9 | **No service levels anywhere.** §1.5, §1.6, §2.2 and §9.3 all reference service levels, an SLA exhibit, and service credits — none exist. | §9.3's "repeatedly misses a critical service level" termination right is unenforceable; no uptime commitment, no credits, no support response times. | Attach an **SLA Exhibit** (uptime %, measurement method, exclusions, support severity/response/resolution targets, escalation). State credits are **not** the sole remedy and that chronic failure (e.g., 3 misses in 6 months, or any month below X%) permits termination without penalty and a pro-rata refund. |
| 10 | **§23 "Records and Customer Assurance" is a heading with no text.** *(p0090)* | Customer has **no audit or assurance right** over Vendor, while §22 gives Vendor a full audit right over Customer — a one-way street. | Draft §23: annual SOC 2 Type II (or ISO 27001) reports; penetration test executive summaries; right to a security questionnaire annually; on-site/remote assessment on reasonable notice or after any Security Incident; retention of records supporting invoices for the term + 3 years and a fee-audit right with refund of overcharges plus audit costs if >5%. |
| 11 | **No security or data-processing exhibit attached.** §2.2 references a "security exhibit"; §13.4 references "testing authorized by the security exhibit"; §15.2 incorporates a DPA. | Core security and privacy commitments are unincorporated. §17.1 is a good baseline but does not cover subprocessors, data residency, key management, or pen testing. | Attach both before signature. Add to §17: (a) prior notice and objection right for new subprocessors; (b) data residency/location restrictions; (c) Customer right to conduct or commission penetration testing annually; (d) Vendor bears notification, credit-monitoring, forensics, and remediation costs for Vendor-caused incidents (tie to §21.2 "direct damages"). |
| 12 | **§16 is missing 16.3 and 16.4.** *(p0067)* | No standard exclusions and, critically, **no compelled-disclosure procedure** — Vendor could produce Customer Confidential Information in response to a subpoena without notice to Customer. | Add: standard exclusions (public without breach, independently developed, rightfully received, already known); and a compelled-disclosure clause requiring prompt notice (where lawful), reasonable cooperation in seeking protective treatment, and disclosure of the minimum required portion. |
| 13 | **§4 heading promises "Affiliate Orders"; no mechanism drafted.** §12 is missing 12.1–12.2 and "Authorized Users" (used in §1.3) is undefined. | Affiliates cannot order; ambiguity over who may use the Services and who is liable. | Add §4.2: Customer Affiliates may execute Order Forms referencing this Agreement; each is a separate contract between Vendor and that Affiliate; Customer is not liable for Affiliate obligations (or is jointly liable, if commercially agreed); Customer may enforce on an Affiliate's behalf. Add an "Authorized Users" definition covering Customer, Affiliate, and contractor personnel. |
| 14 | **§3 has one subsection only.** *(p0017)* | No key-personnel commitments, no subcontractor approval right, no non-solicitation protection for Customer's staff, no continuous-improvement or reporting obligations. | Add: named key personnel with no removal without notice/replacement of equal calibre; Customer right to require removal of any Vendor personnel; **prior written notice of material subcontractors and the right to object on reasonable grounds**; flow-down of §§15–17 and §26; mutual non-solicit carve-out consistent with §12.3. |
| 15 | **§14.1 "improve the Services" licence.** *(p0057)* | Broader than the §15.1 limits on Customer Data use; could be read to permit product development using Customer material. | Narrow to "…to provide, secure, and support the Services **for Customer**, and to improve the Services provided that such improvement does not involve use of Customer Data other than as permitted by Section 15.1." |
| 16 | **§1.3 telemetry carve-out.** *(p0005)* | "Anonymized operational telemetry" is excluded from Customer Data without a standard for de-identification or a re-identification ban. | Add: de-identification must be irreversible under recognised standards; Vendor shall not attempt re-identification; aggregated data must not identify Customer or be disclosed in a form attributable to Customer. |
| 17 | **§9.1 cure period up to 90 days.** *(p0036)* | Too long for security, confidentiality, privacy, and unlawful-conduct breaches. | Carve out: no extension for breaches of §§15, 16, 17, 26, or for non-payment; those remain at 30 days (or, for a material Security Incident, immediate termination under §9.3). |
| 18 | **§18 insurance limits.** *(p0072)* | E&O at USD 2M is low for a $2M/year analytics platform; notice of cancellation only "to the extent available." | E&O to USD 5M; retain cyber at USD 5M (higher if sensitive/personal data volumes are large); require Customer as additional insured on CGL; waiver of subrogation; **30 days' written notice** of cancellation or material reduction (10 days for non-payment); tail coverage for claims-made policies for 2 years post-term. |
| 19 | **No source-code escrow / continuity on insolvency.** | §9.2 permits termination on insolvency but leaves Customer with no continuity path for a business-critical hosted service. | Consider escrow of source code and build/deployment materials with release on insolvency, cessation of support, or uncured material breach; alternatively a hosted-continuity commitment (third-party hosting arrangement). |
| 20 | **No survival clause.** | Ambiguity as to which obligations continue post-termination. | Add §30.9 listing survival: §§1, 10, 11, 13.2, 14, 15, 16, 19.5, 20, 21, 22.3, 24, 25, 28, 29, 30. |

---

## TIER 3 — Cleanup / drafting defects

| Clause | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| §2.2 ×2 *(p0013, p0014)* | Duplicate numbering | Renumber after deleting the exclusivity clause |
| §9.3 *(p0038)* | Cross-refers to non-existent §20.5 | Resolved by the Section 20 rewrite above |
| §29.3 *(p0114)* | Notice copies go to `legal@northwind.example` and `legal@brightline.example` — **neither party is Northwind or Brightline** | Insert correct Meridian and Copperleaf legal-notice addresses. Confirm no other party's terms were copied into this draft. |
| Preamble *(p0001)* | Vendor described as a **New York corporation** but named "Copperleaf Technology **Ltd.**" | Verify entity type, jurisdiction of incorporation, and exact legal name against good-standing records before signature |
| §1.5 *(p0007)* | "Fees" excludes one-time implementation charges | See item 8 — shrinks cap and refund base |
| §10.1 *(p0042)* | "after any agreed transition period" with no default | Tie to the new §11.1 twelve-month transition period as the default |
| §11.2 *(p0046)* | Return only "within thirty days after Customer's request" — unclear whether the right exists during the term | Add: "at any time during the term and for twelve (12) months thereafter," plus self-service export throughout the term |
| §21.3 *(p0084)* | Excluded Claims omit breach of §19.3 (malicious code / open-source contamination) and §26 (anti-bribery, sanctions, export) | Add both |
| §7.3 *(p0028)* | Good dispute-withholding right, but no express bar on suspension for disputed amounts | Add: "Vendor shall not suspend, degrade, or terminate the Services on account of any amount disputed in good faith under this Section, or on account of undisputed amounts unless overdue by more than thirty (30) days after a second written notice." |
| §22.1 *(p0087)* | Vendor audit right lacks a self-help remedy limit | Confirm Vendor may not use audit findings to suspend Services; add "Vendor's sole remedy for underpayment is payment of the shortfall under §22.2." |
| §28.3 *(p0110)* | Escalation is a condition precedent for "ordinary commercial claims" | Acceptable; confirm the carve-out for urgent relief also covers termination notices |

---

## Recommended negotiation sequence

1. **Non-negotiable deletions (Tier 1, items 1–7):** §2.1, §2.2 (exclusivity), §11.1, §12.4, §13.1, §19.2, §21.1. These are internally inconsistent with the rest of the draft; the cleanest framing to Vendor is that they appear to be drafting errors or residue from another template (consistent with the wrong notice addresses in §29.3).
2. **Section 20 rewrite (item 8)** — the absence of any Vendor indemnity is the largest single unpriced risk.
3. **Attach the three missing exhibits** (SLA, Security, DPA) — the Agreement expressly references all three and is incomplete without them.
4. **Draft §23** to give Customer symmetric assurance rights.
5. Tier 3 items can be swept in a single clean-up markup.

Happy to produce a full redline on request. Please also confirm (a) whether personal data will be processed and whether any of it crosses borders, so we can size the DPA/SCC requirement, and (b) the actual expected annual spend, so we can calibrate the liability cap and insurance limits.
